Railway Coil Spring Selection: Why Free Height Is Not Enough

Specify a railway coil spring through load-deflection behavior, installed geometry and seat interfaces rather than free height alone.

2026-11-14 · Suspension · Ma'anshan Railwheel Industrial Technology Co., Ltd.

The purchasing error hidden in a dimension

Two springs can have the same free height and outside diameter yet behave differently under load. Bar diameter, active turns, end construction and material condition influence the relationship between force and deflection. The purchasing definition must therefore connect geometry to functional requirements. A catalog photograph may identify a spring family, but it cannot establish that a replacement will preserve the approved suspension characteristics.

Use load points with explicit reference conditions

Ask the designer to identify the forces required at specified compressed heights, their tolerances and the measurement conditions. Distinguish nominal operating points from limiting conditions. If a supplier reports spring rate, confirm the interval over which it is evaluated; a single rate value does not replace a defined curve where contact or progressive behavior matters. For an approximately linear range, the change in force divided by the change in deflection provides a useful consistency check, not a complete design validation.

Engineering principle: sensitivity is not proportional to size

For an ideal close-coiled cylindrical spring made from circular bar, the familiar elastic estimate is k = G d^4 / (8 D^3 n), with shear modulus G, bar diameter d, mean coil diameter D and active turns n. Consistent units are essential. The fourth-power dependence on bar diameter explains why matching only free height and outside diameter can miss a major stiffness difference. This simplified model excludes effects such as coil contact, changing active turns, detailed end conditions and the complete vehicle dynamics. It is a way to ask better questions, not a railway spring approval calculation. The drawing and required measured behavior remain the purchasing authority.

Check the occupied envelope, not just the unloaded outline

The spring must fit its seats and remain compatible with its surroundings through the approved working range. Confirm end form, seat contacts, locating features, permitted lateral movement and the internal and external envelope. Record clearance requirements from the assembly design. Do not derive a permissible compressed height by counting visible gaps on a used sample, because wear, residual set and unknown original construction can make that sample misleading.

Separate a quotation comparison from design approval

A bidder should return a drawing revision, material proposal and compliance statement tied to the same load schedule. List deviations rather than hiding them inside a supplier drawing. A lower price for a spring with a different functional baseline is not a comparable offer. EN 13298 is a relevant scope reference for steel helical suspension springs; the actual contract must identify the applicable edition and project requirements. No generic article can approve a spring substitution.

Close the loop at receipt

Incoming inspection should connect the physical marking to the ordered part and its required dimensional and load records. Confirm whether the supplier tested individual springs, a sample or a group, and whether that coverage matches the purchase order. Keep questionable items segregated until the authorized reviewer resolves discrepancies. Installation and service release belong to the controlled maintenance process, not the purchasing checklist.

Application scenario

Illustrative scenario: a freight depot requests a spring matching an old spring's free height. The bidder returns the same outer dimensions but a different load schedule. The correct next step is to retrieve the approved suspension specification and compare force at the specified working heights. It is not to install the new spring and judge equivalence from vehicle appearance. The scenario explains a decision process, not a Railwheel delivery record.

Frequently asked questions

Does equal free height mean equal spring rate?

No. Free height is one geometric characteristic. The required load-deflection behavior and complete spring construction must also match the approved specification.

Can a supplier choose a close alternative?

An alternative must be declared as a deviation and approved by the responsible engineering authority before it becomes an accepted supply definition.
